title: Literal encoding round trip
statement: For any literal $\ell=(v,b)$, where $v\in\mathbb N$ and $b\in\{0,1\}$, and any finite bit string $r$, parsing the concatenation $1^{v+1}0b\,r$ returns the literal $\ell$ and remainder $r$.
hypotheses_covered: $\ell$ is a literal with variable index in $\mathbb N$ and polarity bit in $\{0,1\}$
replaced:
Let $\ell = (v, b)$ be a literal with variable index $v \in \mathbb{N}$ and polarity bit
$b \in \{0,1\}$, whose binary encoding is $1^{v+1}0b$, and let $r$ be any bit string. The
literal parser, which on an input of the form $1^{k+1}0cy$ returns the literal $(k,c)$ with
remainder $y$ and fails on every other input, succeeds on $1^{v+1}0b\,r$ and returns $\ell$
with remainder $r$.
